approved_list.document: Form W-2 from each employer (yours and, if filing jointly, your spouse's), including any employer you left during the year, plus any corrected Form W-2c
Form 1099-B (or the broker's consolidated or substitute statement) from each brokerage or fund company, plus purchase and sale records for any sale not reported on a form or with basis not reported

Form 1099-DA (if received), plus the client's own records for every digital asset sold, exchanged, spent, or used to pay fees: date and time acquired, cost basis, date disposed, and proceeds or fair market value in U.S. dollars

Form 1099-G from the state or local tax agency showing state or local income tax refunds, credits, or offsets (including amounts applied to estimated tax, offset, or donated) and the tax year of the refund; plus the prior-year return or Schedule A for that tax year if not on file

Closing statement from the home purchase (settlement statement, Closing Disclosure, ALTA statement, or HUD-1), including the buyer's side showing points, prorated property taxes, any mortgage insurance or VA funding fee paid at closing, and settlement costs

Schedule K-1 from each partnership, S corporation, estate, or trust in which the client held an interest or was a beneficiary at any time during 2026 (a separate K-1 for each entity), plus any Schedule K-3 a partnership or S corporation sends

For each rental real estate property: rents and other amounts received (including the fair market value of any property or services received as rent), expenses paid, the number of days rented at a fair rental price and the number of days of personal use, purchase, improvement, and prior depreciation records, a dated mileage log if car expenses are claimed, and any Forms 1099-MISC or 1099-K received

Overtime records and how the employer reported them: Form W-2 with code TT (qualified overtime compensation, the FLSA-required premium above the regular rate); Form 1099-NEC box 1d or Form 1099-MISC in the rare case the client was an FLSA employee treated as a contractor; corrected Form W-2c if the code TT amount is missing or understated (a substitute Form 4852 does not count); pay stubs or payroll records to check the amount

follow_up_questions.question: Did you itemize deductions on last year's return instead of taking the standard deduction?
